confidence_notes: The FX rate comes from an RBA search result (AUD/USD 0.6720 at 4.00 pm on 18 Nov 2026). I did not open the RBA table directly. Food and coffee anchors come from search snippets of a crowdsourced cost-of-living site (MyLifeElsewhere, Numbeo-style data). Its snapshots disagree: beer is about $1.7-1.8, cappuccino about $1.5-1.6, and an inexpensive meal about $1.7-2.4. I set the anchors slightly above these averages to reflect tourist-area (ghat) pricing. I ran no searches for the mid-range meal, cocktail or wine, so the two-person mid-range meal is an estimate scaled from the inexpensive meal and Indian tourist-city norms. Cocktail and wine are set relative to beer, because alcohol is limited and heavily taxed in Varanasi and tourist-area menus are thin. Wine is about 2x beer and cocktail about 2.3x beer. All accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge of Indian pilgrimage-city lodging. I did not search for accommodation or check any listings.
comparable_city_reasoning: Compared with other mid-sized North Indian tourist and pilgrimage cities such as Agra, Jaipur and Rishikesh, with a slight adjustment for Varanasi's ghat-area tourist pricing. Varanasi is cheaper than Delhi on the cost-of-living snapshots found.
